title: IDD resolved distribution selection
description: Reports the immutable set selected for a repository and session, the rule that selected it, and any required recovery action without changing state.

schemaVersion.description: Selects the resolved-selection report contract version.

repository.description: Names the exact owner/repo for which the report applies, or is null when no repository applies, including outside Git. Exact matching prevents a report for one repository from applying to another; resolver children enforce it at run time.

session.description: Identifies the session whose immutable selection is reported.

binding.description: Reports whether this session already has a binding. A `session-bound` verdict requires `bound` (rule 3); `bound` requires a verdict of `session-bound`, `preparation-missing`, `migration-required`, or `not-verified-usable` (rule 13).

verdict.description: Reports the first of the following values that holds, in this order: `not-verified-usable` when a manifest fact fails or receipt is `conflict`; `migration-required` when installed instructions have unknown provenance or bytes that differ from manifest files, or source is `legacy-receipt` or `unknown`, or receipt is `unsupported-legacy`; `preparation-missing`; `session-bound` when session.binding is `bound`; `pin-preserved` when source is `repository-pin`; `distinct-builds` when compared packageVersion strings are equal but commits differ; otherwise `coherent-candidate`. `coherent-candidate` means every component shares one sourceCommit and carries the files and digest required by child A. `distinct-builds` is not compatibility: a matching package version or bin name alone is insufficient. `not-verified-usable` covers missing commands, incompatible flags, schema or markers, absent identity, schema-invalid manifests including missing or unknown manifest provenance, equal sourceCommit with different component digests, and components from mixed commits; mixed commits are never compatible. An identity absent only because installed instructions have unknown or mismatched provenance is `migration-required`. `pin-preserved` means an explicit repository pin wins over a newer global default. `session-bound` keeps an existing session set when the current link moves. `migration-required` never invents an identity. `preparation-missing` identifies a proved set whose required preparation is absent.

sourceCommit.description: Proves identity. Names the full source commit from which every component was built.

components.description: Groups the immutable instructions, skill bundle, and helper components.

instructions.description: Proves identity. Defines the complete installed instruction component rooted at idd-template/.

location.description: Proves usability only. Gives a commit-pinned forge URL whose path names the instructions component root; its commit must equal sourceCommit.

provenance.description: Proves identity. Records how the instruction component bytes were read and their source commit.

kind.description: Records the provenance method as checkout or archive; it does not change build identity.

commit.description: Proves identity. Records the source commit and must equal sourceCommit.

files.description: Proves identity. Lists every instructions file relative to the component root with its SHA-256.

path.description: Proves identity. Names one non-empty relative file path using slash separators without a parent-directory segment or line terminator.

sha256.description: Proves identity. Gives the lowercase SHA-256 of this file's bytes.

digest.description: Proves identity. Hashes the bytewise path-sorted listing of file SHA-256 values and paths.

selected.description: Reports the selected identity for `coherent-candidate`, `pin-preserved`, `session-bound`, and `preparation-missing`, and is null for `distinct-builds`, `not-verified-usable`, and `migration-required` (rule 1). For `preparation-missing`, it identifies the set to prepare. Identity equality is decided by sourceCommit with each component digest and provenance.commit; location and invocation prove usability only. `compatibility: compatible` requires a non-null selected identity (rule 11).

previousVerifiedSet.description: Holds the last set verified and compatible for this repository. When compatibility is `unknown`, a non-null previousVerifiedSet keeps that identity available; null is allowed when no verified set has existed, so no identity is invented.

packageVersion.description: Informational package version used for comparison, never an identity key. The `distinct-builds` verdict requires a non-null packageVersion (rule 6).

preparation.description: `prepared` means every file of the selected set is present in the prepared-set layout; the report does not name that layout owner. `preparation-missing` means at least one file is absent. `not-applicable` means selected is null. Rule 2 requires `prepared` for `coherent-candidate`, `pin-preserved`, and `session-bound`, `preparation-missing` for that verdict, and `not-applicable` exactly when selected is null.

compatibility.description: `compatible` means every compatibility check passed and requires non-null selected (rule 11). `incompatible` means a check failed and requires verdict `not-verified-usable` (rule 7). `unknown` means a check could not run and fails before any workflow mutation.

source.description: `repository-pin` means an explicit repository pin and requires a non-null repository plus one of the allowed pin-preserved, session-bound, preparation-missing, migration-required, or not-verified-usable verdicts (rule 14). `repository-local` names local instructions, which keep precedence in routing. `global-current` is the set selected by the current global link or default when no repository pin or session binding applies. `installed-bundle` is the immutable bundle recorded by a verified installation. `legacy-receipt` and `unknown` require `migration-required` or `not-verified-usable` (rule 10). `pin-preserved` requires `repository-pin` (rule 4).

recovery.description: `none` means no action. `prepare` means required preparation is missing and holds exactly for verdict `preparation-missing` (rule 5). `migrate` means migration is required, whatever the source, and holds exactly for `migration-required` (rule 9). `reselect` means the chosen set is no longer verified and requires `not-verified-usable` (rule 8), whether bound, pinned, or globally current.

receipt.description: Reports persisted receipt state. `readReceipt` and `writeReceipt` in `src/scripts/user-global-receipt.mts` use the existing no-follow read guard and receipt guard for any persisted state; this schema adds no guard. `unsupported-legacy` requires `migration-required` or `not-verified-usable`, and `conflict` requires `not-verified-usable` (rule 12).

status.description: `verified` means a receipt exists and passes the receipt guard. `absent` means no receipt exists. `unsupported-legacy` means the resolver cannot use the existing legacy format. `conflict` means a receipt disagrees with the selected identity or another receipt.

mutation.description: Holds only `none`; inspection performs no mutation.
